name: Johanna Kretzschmar
headline: Data Product Leader | BI & Data Strategy | Turning Data into Business Impact
summary:
I’m a Data Product Leader who brings people, business and technology together to make data truly useful. 
I lead with clarity, empathy and a strong sense for collaboration—turning complex challenges into data products that empower teams and support confident decision making.

My background is rooted in business, BI and analytics, and over the years I’ve learned that the most powerful data products are built when business and technology truly understand each other – and when teams feel safe to explore, question and learn.

In my current role at Sky, I lead data products that support key decisions across finance, commercial and operational teams – from migration analytics and KPI frameworks to self-service analytics platforms and scenario simulations. 
I love taking complex problems, bringing the right people together and shaping them into clear, usable and trustworthy data products that make everyday work easier.

As a leader, I focus on alignment, clarity and empowerment. 
I create structure where it’s needed, but I also give teams the space to contribute ideas and grow. I’m comfortable leading without formal authority, building bridges between stakeholders and helping everyone see the bigger picture behind the numbers.

What drives me most is this:
- enabling people to make better decisions with confidence
- turning data into a strategic asset instead of a by-product
- building a culture where data, collaboration and curiosity go hand in hand

If you’re working on challenges around data products, governance, BI or data-driven transformation, I’m always happy to connect and exchange ideas.

company.name: Sky Deutschland GmbH
company.tagline: A job you ❤️ to talk about
company.description:
With 23 million customers across six countries, Sky is Europe’s leading media and entertainment company and is proud to be part of the Comcast group. Our 34,000 employees help connect our customers to the very best entertainment, sports, news, arts and to our own local, original content. Following the success of Sky originals like Chernobyl, we plan to double our investment in original content by 2024. 
We’re also developing a new TV and movie studio, Sky Studios Elstree, which is expected to lead to the creation of over 2,000 new jobs and generate an additional £3 billion of production investment in UK creative sector in the first five years alone. 
Our technology allows Sky customers to watch what they want, when they want, how they want and connects millions of people to content they love. And our online streaming service, Sky Ticket, brings viewers all the enjoyment of Sky with the flexibility of a contract-free service. 
We also believe that a company of our scale has a responsibility that goes beyond our business, and into the community. We recently announced a series of commitments to help tackle racial injustice and improve diversity and inclusion. To ensure the commitments are delivered, Sky will invest £10million per year across its markets for each of the next three years. We’re committed to being Europe’s first net zero carbon entertainment company by 2030 – two decades before we have to – and we’re an inclusive employer recognised by The Times and Stonewall for our commitment to diversity.
